You've probably heard the famous story that when Charlie Parker was starting out to play he went to one of these jam sessions and tried to get in with sort of the big company, and he didn't do very well. And there's a story that Jo Jones unscrewed his cymbal and threw it on the floor.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Buster Smith is there and he's still alive. You could not get that out of that. ... The "Father" He was part of Charlie Parker's.

ctx.x: Bass too, but I mean this is a thing, this is a wedding now. Then Walter Page gave up his band and he joined the band along with Dan Minor and Buster Smith and what have you. And you must remember, I can explain to you why the rhythm section of Basie's band the first time - he always had a sax section and a brass section. Bennie Moten played one and three. Walter Page played on two and four; but when they wedded together you had one, two, three, four. The two mediums met, from the one and three, one and three, as…
Who was drumming with Walter Page's Blue Devils, do you remember?
